q: Does Qiskit's default transpile/routing preserve the Figure-5 depth guarantee (2n+4) under realistic hardware connectivity constraints such as heavy-hex or linear-nearest-neighbour, and if not, what is the depth overhead as a function of n?
basis: Our measured depth of 2n+4 at n=4,5 was on all-to-all logical connectivity. The MAJ/UMA gates touch (A_{i-1}, B_i, A_i) triples which are not neighbours on most hardware couplings; SWAP insertion could substantially inflate depth and reshape any speedup argument versus the VBE adder.
next_steps: Re-run verify_adder.py after qiskit.transpile(coupling_map=...) for a linear chain and heavy-hex; fit depth(n) empirically and compare to the 2n+4 target.

q: Qiskit's depth() counts X gates but still returned 2n+4, matching the paper's 2n-1 Toffoli slices + 5 CNOT slices. Are the negations (2n-4 of them) actually absorbed into the end-cap CNOT time-slices as the paper implicitly claims, or is this a coincidence that would break if the X placements were shifted inside the interior of the ripple?
basis: The paper enumerates 2n-1 Toffoli time-slices + 5 CNOT time-slices for depth 2n+4 and never explicitly slots the negations in. We got depth 2n+4 anyway, which suggests the negations happen to parallelise with CNOTs on other wires. But we have not built the explicit slice-by-slice diagram to confirm this is structural rather than fortuitous.
next_steps: Generate a wire-vs-time-slice diagram of the optimized circuit and mark where each X gate lands. Perturb X placements to verify depth robustness.

q: How does the CDKM 1-ancilla optimized adder compare to the VBE n-O(1)-ancilla adder in *noise-robustness*, not just gate count, when both are compiled into a Clifford+T basis and simulated under a depolarising channel of rate p?
basis: The paper proves a resource win (fewer Toffolis, fewer ancillae). But n-1 fewer ancillae also means more re-use of physical qubits inside a single circuit, which changes error-propagation topology. Whether the fewer-gate advantage survives under noise (or whether extra ancillae give VBE a locality benefit) is not addressed by the paper and matters for fault-tolerant use.
next_steps: Implement both adders in the same Qiskit / Aer noise model at n=4,5,6; sweep p in [1e-4, 1e-2]; measure output fidelity vs. p; report Pareto frontier.

q: The Figure-5 pseudocode is explicitly restricted to n >= 4. For n = 2, 3 the paper implicitly falls back to the Figure-4 simple adder or ad-hoc edge cases. What is the true minimum Toffoli/CNOT/NOT count for CDKM-style 1-ancilla adders at n = 2, 3, and does the closed-form (2n-1, 5n-3, 2n-4) actually extend below n=4 or does it break?
basis: We measured the *simple* adder at n=3 and got 6 Toffoli / 13 CNOT / depth 17, which does *not* fit 2n-1 = 5. The paper never gives a Figure-5-style optimized construction for these small n. A brute-force search or hand construction could establish whether the extrapolation of the linear formulas is tight, over-counted, or genuinely impossible.
next_steps: Brute-force enumerate Clifford+T circuits on 2n+2 = 6, 8 qubits with Toffoli, CNOT, X gates up to length ~15 that realise the 2- or 3-bit adder truth table; find the true optimum and compare to 2n-1, 5n-3, 2n-4.

q: The paper claims the 3-CNOT UMA (Figure 2b) is required to reach the optimised 2n+4 depth. Can the 2-CNOT UMA (Figure 2a) be depth-optimised through commutation and re-scheduling to match, or is there a genuine circuit-topological barrier that forces the 3-CNOT variant?
basis: Our Figure-4 implementation with the 2-CNOT UMA measured depth 17, 22, 27 at n=3,4,5 (a slope of 5 per unit n) versus the optimized 12, 14, 16 (slope 2). The paper asserts the 2-CNOT UMA cannot be re-arranged to close this gap, but doesn't prove it. A pass over the 2-CNOT variant with an aggressive gate-commutation optimiser would test the claim.
next_steps: Apply qiskit's CommutativeCancellation + template-matching passes to the Figure-4 (2-CNOT-UMA) circuit; report the best achievable depth as a function of n. If depth(n) does not collapse to 2n+O(1), that is strong empirical evidence for the paper's claim.
